draft.title: Surface area of a cone
card: A cone has a circular base of radius \(r\) and a curved surface. The slant height \(s\) is the distance from the tip down the side of the cone to the edge of the base.
The curved surface has area \(\pi r s\). Use the slant height \(s\), not the vertical height \(h\).
A closed cone also has a circular base of area \(\pi r^{2}\). So the total surface area is \(SA = \pi r^{2} + \pi r s\).
A closed cone has radius 3 cm and slant height 5 cm. Base: \(\pi \times 3^{2} = 9\pi\). Curved: \(\pi \times 3 \times 5 = 15\pi\). Total: \(24\pi \approx 75.4\) cm\(^{2}\).
draft.remember: Closed cone: base \(\pi r^{2}\) plus curved surface \(\pi r s\), using slant height.

a.q: A closed cone has radius 4 cm and slant height 7 cm. What is its total surface area, in terms of \(\pi\)?
a.why: Base: \(\pi \times 4^{2} = 16\pi\). Curved: \(\pi \times 4 \times 7 = 28\pi\). Total \(44\pi\). Giving \(28\pi\) leaves out the base, which a closed cone has.
a.clue: A closed cone has a base as well as a curved surface.

b.q: A closed cone has radius 6 cm and vertical height 8 cm. What is its total surface area, in terms of \(\pi\)?
b.why: First find the slant height: \(s = \sqrt{6^{2} + 8^{2}} = 10\). Then \(SA = \pi \times 6^{2} + \pi \times 6 \times 10 = 36\pi + 60\pi = 96\pi\). Using \(h = 8\) as the slant height gives \(84\pi\), which is wrong.
b.clue: The formula needs the slant height, which is not given.

wants.brief: A cone with the radius \(r\) marked on the circular base, the slant height \(s\) marked along the side from the tip to the edge of the base, and the vertical height \(h\) marked from the tip straight down to the centre of the base as a dashed line.
wants.why: It shows the slant height apart from the vertical height.

proposal.title: Surface area of a cone
card: A cone has a circular base of radius \(r\) and a curved surface. The slant height \(s\) is the distance from the tip down the side of the cone to the edge of the base.
The vertical height \(h\), the radius \(r\) and the slant height \(s\) form a right-angled triangle. So by Pythagoras, \(s = \sqrt{r^{2} + h^{2}}\).
The curved surface has area \(\pi r s\), using \(s\), not \(h\). A closed cone also has a base of area \(\pi r^{2}\), so \(SA = \pi r^{2} + \pi r s\).
For example, a closed cone has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm. Then \(s = \sqrt{9 + 16} = 5\). Base \(9\pi\), curved \(15\pi\), so the total is \(24\pi \approx 75.4\) cm\(^{2}\).
proposal.remember: Closed cone: \(SA = \pi r^{2} + \pi r s\), with the slant height \(s\), not \(h\).

a.q: A closed cone has radius 4 cm and slant height 7 cm. What is its total surface area, in terms of \(\pi\)?
a.why: Base: \(\pi \times 4^{2} = 16\pi\). Curved: \(\pi \times 4 \times 7 = 28\pi\). The total is \(44\pi\). Giving \(28\pi\) leaves out the base, which a closed cone has.
a.clue: A closed cone has a base as well as a curved surface.

b.q: A closed cone has radius 6 cm and vertical height 8 cm. What is its total surface area, in terms of \(\pi\)?
b.why: First find the slant height: \(s = \sqrt{36 + 64} = 10\). Then \(SA = 36\pi + 60\pi = 96\pi\). Using \(h = 8\) in place of the slant height gives \(36\pi + 48\pi = 84\pi\), which is wrong.
b.clue: Which length does the formula need, and is it given?
